To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Aria 3 service, October 2026

Dana, I said last month that I would report back once my writer had been through a real trial. It has now survived eight days of a civil trial, so here is the promised review.

I took my Stenvale Aria 3 to Harbor Point Steno Service on Monday, October 19, and picked it up on Tuesday, October 27. They quoted 10 business days and had it back in six. The original estimate was $285; the final bill was $310, including a battery replacement that I approved beforehand. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment. There was no reimbursement from the court.

The work included a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning, and a firmware update from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1. The internal battery was also replaced. Gloria emailed to say it was holding about 60 percent of its rated capacity and that replacement would be $25, parts and labor. She explicitly said she would not proceed without my approval. I appreciated being asked rather than finding an extra charge at pickup. For what was done, I think $310 was fair. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The important part is how it writes. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight days of trial use, I have not had a recurrence. That is a useful test, though it is still eight days, not a long-term verdict.

The machine also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never received that from anyone else. It gives me something concrete to keep with the machine’s records, and I would like to see more shops do it.

They did provide a loaner, a Stenvale Aria 2. Unfortunately, its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition. I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I reported it to Gloria by email, and she said they would repair the arm before sending it out again. Having a loaner made the turnaround manageable, but it needs to hold its position without help from my stationery.

Communication is the weakness. Their phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the next day about the battery, but that does not make the phone arrangements adequate. For anyone working a Monday docket, those hours are a real limitation. I would not count on being able to reach someone by phone when a problem arises.

For local logistics, Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, with free parking in back.

Dana, based on this visit, I would trust Gloria with another Aria 3, and I would use the shop again. The repair has held up under the work I needed it to do, the price was reasonable, and the documentation was unusually good. I would make arrangements in advance, confirm the loaner is sound, and plan on email rather than dependable phone access. Good technical work deserves credit; the phone situation still needs fixing.

Maureen
